extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 challenge samples meticulously selected by humans. MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.publisher: University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline using eight powerful LLMs as candidate inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Then 16 leading LVLMs are used to gauge the difficulty of the samples and split them to four levels. Finally, strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples collected from six existing benchmarks: two benchmarks focused on natural images (MMBench, SEED) and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge (MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, MathVista).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits from LLM inspectors were retained, indicating that around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer. Following this initial coarse filtering, the sample pool was reduced from 22,401 to 11,607.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline was developed to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet visual dependency and minimal data leakage criteria. Two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs sizing 20B or larger served as inspectors with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Hit counts of all 16 LVLMs were tallied and samples split into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline using eight powerful LLMs as candidate inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded. Then 16 leading LVLMs are used to gauge the difficulty of the samples and split them into four levels. Ultimately, strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, IntemLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B. Sixteen LVLMs used for difficulty assessment: GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series, and others.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Future plans to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two primary biases in existing benchmarks: 1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples - answers can be directly inferred from questions/options or world knowledge embedded in LLMs; 2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training, where models can answer visual-necessary questions without visual content due to memorization during training.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark currently contains 1,500 samples. Future work plans to expand into a larger online test set. The paper notes that even with careful curation, maintaining sample visual dependency and reducing data leakage requires ongoing dynamic evaluation methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) across 6 core capabilities: Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, and Mathematics. The benchmark aims to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that require visual understanding.

These open-source LLMs are applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting.
